Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the appellant.
2. Mr. Tarun Pande, Advocate for the respondent no.1/claimant.

3. None present for respondent nos.2 and 3.
4.
This is Money Withdrawal Application IA No.4238 of 2022 moved by the respondent no.1/claimant seeking release of the amount deposited by the appellant before the Tribunal concerned.

entities.text: Money Withdrawal Application IA No.4238 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the appellant would oppose the money withdrawal application on the ground that there was no eyewitness of the accident in question and the respondent no.1/claimant had herself filed the final report of this accident before the Tribunal as documentary evidence, therefore,
there was no negligence on the part.
However, he would admit at Bar that the reasons for filing the final report did not come on record during trial.

6. Learned counsel for respondent no.1/applicant, per contra, would submit that in para 10 of the impugned Award the Tribunal has categorically observed that the manner in which the accident had taken place attracts principle of res ipsa loquitur, therefore, the burden shifts on respondent no.2 i.e.
the owner to prove the manner of accident otherwise than negligence of driver, but the owner has not filed any written statement or evidence.

He would further submit that in the absence of written statement of the owner and driver, the appellant/Insurance Company did not move application u/s 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act to contest the claim petition.

Therefore, the onus that had shifted to the owner of the offending vehicle had further shifted to the appellant/Insurance Company to prove that the accident had not taken place due to negligence of the driver and this onus was not discharged by the appellant/Insurance Company.
He would further submit that the appellant did not summon any witness or adduce any evidence on this point before the Tribunal either.

AO/140/2020 on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24452756/
1 7.

On the money withdrawal application, learned counsel for the respondent no.1 would submit that the respondent no.1/claimant is an old lady, aged about 62 years; that, she is a widower and has no source of income; that, her only son has expired in this unfortunate accident, therefore, she needs money for her survival.
8. In the above facts and circumstances, money withdrawal application is allowed.
Let 50% of the amount, out of the total amount deposited before the Tribunal, be released in favour of the respondent no.1/claimant.
The Tribunal shall deposit the amount so released directly in the bank account of the respondent no.1/claimant, wherefor the respondent no.1/claimant shall provide her account details.
If there is no bank account of the respondent no.1, she will open the same in any nationalized bank and thereafter will provide the details to the Tribunal in order to get the amount of compensation.

9. Summon the LCR.
10. Put up on 19.10.2023 for final hearing.
11.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the Tribunal concerned for information and compliance.

(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 16.08.2023 Rajni AO/140/2020 on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24452756/
